statement.text:
A group G is called of type (F P )∞ if the trivial G-module Z has a resolution by
finitely generated projective G-modules. The class of all groups of type (F P )∞ has
a couple of excellent closure properties with respect to extensions and amalgamated
products (R. Bieri, Homological dimension of discrete groups, Queen Mary College
Math. Notes, London, 1976). Is every periodic group of type (F P )∞ finite? This
is related to the question whether there is an infinite periodic group with a finite
presentation.                                                                  R. Bieri
